nws.synopsis: Isolated light showers will continue for the coastal basin this morning. More widespread moderate showers develop late this evening into Sunday morning, becoming more scattered during the day Sunday before tapering off Sunday afternoon and evening. Dry and warmer for the remainder of the week with highs near to a few degrees below normal each day.
systems: As the upper level trough passes to our north Sunday afternoon, there will be a brief uptick in west/northwest winds over the waters, mountain ridges and desert slopes, with gusts 25-40 mph, weakening overnight into Monday.
Next week, a series of weak, fast-moving ridges and troughs will keep temperatures fluctuating, though gradually increasing by late week to the low to mid-80s regionwide for lower elevations.

nws.aviation: 311730...Multiple cloud layers across the coastal basin today with mid to high clouds in the deserts. Widespread precip moves into the coastal basin after 03Z Sun, bringing vis reductions (3-5SM) as well as cig reductions (2000-3000 ft MSL) under heavier rain. The highest confidence in heavier rain leading to the aforementioned restrictions is in San Diego County. -SHRA possible in the desrts 10- 16Z Sun. Low to moderate confidence on timing of heavier rain occurrence in TAFs. Showers will become scattered after 18Z.

sites.name: Torrey Pines
sites.note: Ridge soaring in a steady W to WNW sea breeze. SW or NW is cross (soarable but not great); only east is over the back. Rare thermal days (1,200 ft+) are flagged as a Thermal day.

sites.name: Little Black
sites.note: Best post-frontal site in the county. West-facing, so offshore mornings are over the back.

sites.name: Blossom Valley
sites.note: Inland thermal site; often lines up with Elsinore.

sites.name: Elsinore
sites.note: East-facing over the lake; its own animal. Launch in the light air before the switch; the west wind then builds the convergence inland (Perris, Hemet, Soboba). XC wants 7-8k over the range during the switch and the same or more inland.

sites.name: Soboba
sites.note: Flight park on the San Jacinto front.

sites.name: Otay Mesa
sites.note: Near the border; XC goes north and east.

sites.name: Whale's V
sites.note: SW-facing bowl across Otay Lakes Rd from Skydive San Diego. Non-permitted, not an SDHGPA site: coordinate with the DZ, never land at the DZ, no north wind at all. Ridge plus thermal site flying; a few hundred feet over launch is a good day, XC on great days. Under the SAN approach (3,500 ft), not part of the rating. Launch and LZ heights are estimates.

sites.name: Laguna / Horse / Fuzz
sites.note: Convergence sites: Horse faces west, Laguna faces east over the desert, Fuzz is flown on the same convergence. Horse and Laguna are scored on their own and the better one is shown. The rating only says whether the setup is there; where and when the convergence sits, and the morning winds, are for you to check.

sites.name: Santa Barbara (Skyport)
sites.note: South-facing front range above Santa Barbara; launch sits above the marine layer, so thermals are measured from the slopes at launch height. Sundowners and other real north winds are over the back. The range and a capping inversion near ridge height squeeze onshore S-SE flow (venturi: stronger and gustier at the ridgeline than the models show) but block a north wind aloft when the lapse rate is strong.

sites.name: Owens Valley (Walt's Point)
sites.note: Watch only: shows when it rates 5. Advanced pilots only. Morning site with very strong thermals, cloudbase 13-20k. Needs light winds; west wind over the Sierra is a no-go. PGs don't fly it June to early September.
